title: apiome import example corpus manifest
description: Machine-readable contract for every file under apiome-ui/examples/ (IXH-1.1, #5087). One entry per corpus file declares what the file demonstrates, whether it is valid, which adapter must claim it, and what detection/import outcome it is expected to produce. README.md files are documentation and are not corpus entries.

$schema.description: Relative pointer to this schema so editors validate the manifest in place.

manifest_version.description: Manifest contract version; bump only on breaking shape changes.

directories.description: Per-directory human-index metadata (label, category, paradigm, detection marker) used to regenerate the examples README. Every entry path's directory must appear here.

entries.description: One entry per corpus file, sorted by path.

label.description: Human display name of the format family, e.g. "OpenAPI 3.x".

category.description: README grouping section for the directory.

paradigm.description: Canonical API paradigm the format maps to (e.g. rest, rpc, event, data_schema, message, soap, graph).

marker.description: The content marker format detection keys on, in Markdown.

path.description: File path relative to apiome-ui/examples/, POSIX separators.

format.description: Format family key the file belongs to (selection key for load_corpus(format=...)), e.g. openapi, graphql, cobolcopybook.

adapter_key.description: Registry key of the ImportSource adapter that must claim the file (e.g. grpc for protobuf/), or null when no adapter is expected to handle it.

validity_class.description: valid: well-formed, must import cleanly. invalid: malformed on purpose, must be rejected with a useful error. adversarial: crafted to confuse detection or normalization. scale: stresses size/volume limits.

expected_detection.description: The detection contract: format detection must report this format key for the file with at least min_confidence among its candidates. min_confidence 0 means no detection guarantee (e.g. deliberately malformed input).

format.description: Detection format key (may be more specific than `format`, e.g. openapi-3.1, asyncapi-2, json-schema-2020-12).

features.description: Tags for what the file demonstrates (spec keywords keep native casing, e.g. oneOf; concepts are kebab-case, e.g. occurs-depending-on). Tests select fixtures by these instead of hard-coding paths.

expected_outcome.description: What a full import of the file must do: imports (clean), rejects (clear error, no partial import), or imports_with_warnings (imports but reports fidelity warnings).

source.description: Where the file came from (hand-authored, or an upstream project name).

license.description: SPDX license identifier covering the file's content.

provenance.description: One-sentence origin story for the file.

notes.description: Optional free-text caveats, e.g. known detection deviations the hardening epics must reconcile.
